sections.name: Free GPU & Notebook Compute
sections.whatEntriesLookLike: Platform name, hardware specs, weekly/monthly free limits, and sign-up requirements.
sections.whyWorthSection: Developers need accessible compute for testing LLMs and ML models without upfront hardware costs.

sections.name: Free Vector Databases
sections.whatEntriesLookLike: Database name, free tier storage limits, concurrency limits, and managed vs self-hosted status.
sections.whyWorthSection: Essential for RAG applications, and free tiers allow prototyping without infrastructure overhead.

sections.name: Free MCP Servers Directory
sections.whatEntriesLookLike: Server name, supported AI clients (Cursor, Claude), functionality, and GitHub repository link.
sections.whyWorthSection: MCP is the new standard for connecting AI agents to external tools; a curated directory saves hours of discovery.

sections.name: Free Hosting & Deployment Tiers
sections.whatEntriesLookLike: Platform name, free tier limits (build minutes, bandwidth, sleep rules), and ideal use cases.
sections.whyWorthSection: Developers need to deploy AI wrappers, bots, and APIs for free before committing to paid infrastructure.

sections.name: Free Student & OSS Credit Programs
sections.whatEntriesLookLike: Program name, eligibility criteria, credit amount, and covered services.
sections.whyWorthSection: Students and OSS maintainers often lack funding; these programs provide thousands of dollars in cloud credits.

sections.name: Free AI Courses & Learning Paths
sections.whatEntriesLookLike: Course title, provider, duration, and certification availability.
sections.whyWorthSection: Continuous learning is critical in AI; curated free courses help users upskill without financial barriers.

sections.name: Free Voice & TTS Models
sections.whatEntriesLookLike: Model or platform name, free tier limits (characters/month), and local vs cloud execution.
sections.whyWorthSection: Voice AI is booming, and developers need to know which tools offer viable free tiers or open-source local alternatives.

sections.name: System Prompt & Cursor Rules Collections
sections.whatEntriesLookLike: Collection name, target IDE (Cursor, Windsurf), and specific use case (e.g., React, Security).
sections.whyWorthSection: High-quality prompts and IDE rules dramatically improve AI coding agent output; sharing them accelerates developer workflows.

sections.name: AI Benchmark Leaderboards
sections.whatEntriesLookLike: Leaderboard name, ranking methodology (Elo, static datasets), and tracked modalities.
sections.whyWorthSection: Model performance changes weekly; centralized leaderboards help developers choose the best model for their specific task.

sections.name: Free AI Newsletters & Changelogs
sections.whatEntriesLookLike: Newsletter name, frequency, subscriber count, and primary focus (e.g., research, tools).
sections.whyWorthSection: The AI landscape moves too fast for manual tracking; curated newsletters are the most efficient way to stay updated.

sections.name: Free CI / CD Tiers
sections.whatEntriesLookLike: Platform name, free build minutes per month, concurrency limits, and runner types.
sections.whyWorthSection: Automated testing and deployment are essential, and free CI tiers enable hobbyists and startups to maintain quality without cost.

sections.name: Free Auth, DB & Storage Tiers
sections.whatEntriesLookLike: Service name, free tier limits (MAU, storage GB, bandwidth), and core features included.
sections.whyWorthSection: Modern apps require backend services; these free tiers provide production-ready auth, database, and storage for early-stage projects.

sections.name: Free AI Datasets
sections.whatEntriesLookLike: Dataset repository name, size, modalities supported, and licensing.
sections.whyWorthSection: Data is the fuel for AI; direct links to high-quality, free datasets accelerate fine-tuning and RAG development.

sections.name: Free AI Browser Extensions
sections.whatEntriesLookLike: Extension name, browser compatibility, core functionality, and privacy model.
sections.whyWorthSection: Browser extensions bring AI directly into the user's daily workflow without requiring app switches.

sections.name: Free AI Image & Video Generation APIs
sections.whatEntriesLookLike: API provider name, free credit amount, supported models, and rate limits.
sections.whyWorthSection: Multimodal AI is increasingly relevant; free API credits allow developers to prototype image and video features easily.

newToolCategories.name: Prompt Engineering & Management
newToolCategories.justification: As AI workflows mature, developers need tools to version, test, and optimize prompts systematically.

newToolCategories.name: AI Agent Frameworks
newToolCategories.justification: Power users building autonomous workflows need lightweight, local-friendly frameworks to orchestrate multi-agent tasks.

newBookmarkCategories.name: Free Cloud Compute & Notebooks
newBookmarkCategories.justification: Developers frequently need ephemeral, free GPU environments for testing models without local hardware.

newBookmarkCategories.name: Serverless Backend & Database
newBookmarkCategories.justification: Modern AI apps require fast, scalable backends; these free tiers provide production-ready foundations.

newBookmarkCategories.name: AI Benchmark & Leaderboards
newBookmarkCategories.justification: Model performance shifts rapidly; bookmarking authoritative leaderboards helps users make data-driven model choices.

recentFreeTierChanges.event: Hugging Face Inference API free tier changed to focus on CPU inference with a strict $0.10/mo credit limit for free users.
OpenRouter updated free tier limits, now allowing up to 1,000 requests per day for free models if the user has purchased at least 10 credits.
Groq adjusted free tier rate limits to 30 requests per minute, 1,000 requests per day, and 8,000 tokens per minute.
Anthropic expanded its free tier to include Projects, Artifacts, and app connectors for non-paying users.
Gemini CLI launched a new free tier offering 1,000 requests per day, making AI coding more accessible.
Vercel tightened its pricing and free tier limits for serverless functions and bandwidth, marking another adjustment in its ongoing revisions.
Fly.io removed its permanent free tier and introduced new billing line items in early 2026, impacting small hobby projects.
GitHub expanded free access to Copilot and 1TB of cloud storage for verified students via the GitHub Student Developer Pack.
Cloudflare expanded its Workers AI inference at the edge, offering one of the strongest free tiers for small AI projects in 2026.
Codeium (Windsurf) maintains a generous free tier with unlimited autocomplete and chat with codebase context for individual developers.

offlineFirstLaunchData.reason: Provides immediate visibility into top 20 free API quotas and rotation strategies without requiring an internet connection.
A pre-loaded list of 50 essential open-source local AI tools (Ollama models, LM Studio configs) ensures the app is useful even if the user has no network access.
Common stack templates (React, Python, Rust) are available instantly for copy-pasting, providing immediate value on first launch.
Titles, descriptions, and URLs of the top 100 bookmarks are stored locally, allowing search and discovery before the first sync.
Step-by-step offline instructions for installing and configuring local AI runtimes (Ollama, Jan, LM Studio) reduce first-time friction.
